newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SPEED SKATING-NEW SKATE HELPS GERMANY TO WORLD CUP SWEEP.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-NEW SKATE HELPS GERMANY TO WORLD CUP SWEEP.

text.p: Using revolutionary new skates, Gunda Niemann led a German sweep of the top three places in the women's 3,000 metres at a World Cup speed skating event on Saturday.
Niemann, a double gold medallist at the 1992 Olympics and the all-around world champion, clocked a winning time of four minutes 19.70 seconds on the soft Davos ice.
Her team mate Claudia Pechstein was second in 4:22.81 and Anni Friesinger third in 4:23.21.
The competition marked the first time German skaters had used the newly-developed "flap skate" which releases at the heel.
When the skate was first introduced, with great success, by Dutch skaters at a World Cup competition earlier this season, the German Ice Skating Federation had attempted to have it banned.
However, the skate was approved by the International Skating Union and will be allowed in the Olympics.
The decision prompted several countries, including Germany, to try the new skate.
In the men's 1,500m, Jeroen Straathof of the Netherlands won in 1:55.47, edging Japan's Hiroyuki Noake with 1:55.61.
